messages:
anya: Quick sync: ran the continuous-batcher + reshuffle combo on staging. Observed two problems: queue head stalling on tenant eviction, and bursty KV misses when batches land on new nodes. Want to capture decisions here.

kevin: Can you summarise the stall pattern? was it scheduling, admission, or blocking during batch formation?

anya: Short: when a tenant is marked for migration, we pause its inflight admission and drain, but other tenants in same micro-window wait for the stalled slot. That increased P99 by ~300ms even though the moved tenant accounted for ~4% of traffic.

maria: That's the classic head-of-line blocking. Two mitigations: 1) per-tenant logical lanes (so move only affects its lane), or 2) compact windows (reduce coupling by smaller micro-batches). Both have perf/cost tradeoffs.

sam: Per-tenant lanes sound tempting but expensive (state blowup + more GPU context switches). Compact windows increase kernel invocation overhead. Which is preferable?

kevin: Tradeoff matrix we discussed earlier: isolation vs throughput. Options: 
- many narrow lanes -> low interference, higher overhead (more scheduling ops).
- few wide lanes -> high packing efficiency, more interference.

anya: Proposal: hybrid "soft-lanes": group tenants into N lanes by affinity (size/latency class). Default N=8. Admission credits allocated per-lane. Migration marks only the affected lane as "quiescing" rather than whole queue.

josh: How does that interact with continuous coalesce? soft-lanes could reduce batch packing density if tenants are sharded by size. Could hurt token efficiency.

maria: Right. We should bias grouping to preserve packing: put small/short-tail tenants together. Use historical sequence-length histogram as grouping key.

sam: Another idea: leader-fence the batch head. Allow the batch to proceed but replace evicted requests with fast synthetic placeholders if their tenant is under migration. That keeps the pipeline moving while avoiding wasted KV lookups.

kevin: Synthetic placeholders = less coupling but requires requester to handle partial outputs (we'd need a graceful NOP response or requeue). Also complicates tracing.

anya: On KV prefetch: we tested naive prefetch-on-plan and it saturated NIC. Need rate limiter with backpressure signals from node-level prefetch queue. Also prefer prioritising prefetch for tenants with high RPS or large KV reuse.

maria: Implementation sketch: prefetch controller per-node with tokens. Controller exposes: /prefetch/status, /prefetch/request (async), events `prefetch.start`/`prefetch.complete` with tenant_id, bytes. Controller enforces per-node and per-cluster concurrent caps.

sam: Telemetry: emit tags `batch.head_blocked=true|false`, `lane=soft-<n>`, `prefetch.active`, `prefetch.queue_len`. Critical to correlate with P50/P95/P99 and NIC util.

josh: Interface boundary note: scheduler should emit immutable Plan but include hints: lane_id, prefetch_priority, soft_quiesce=true, canary_fraction for migrate. Orchestration consumes Plan and talks to node controllers via RPC.

kevin: Rollout safety: default to no prefetch for Hosted customers for 2 weeks while we collect telemetry, opt-in via feature flag. Dedicated/Private can enable sooner.

maria: Open tradeoffs to capture in RFC: 
- Soft-lanes reduce head-of-line but may reduce packing efficiency and increase token cost.
- Synthetic placeholders keep throughput but add complexity for correctness & tracing.
- Prefetch reduces cold-path latency but adds transient network/memory pressure; needs backpressure and accounting.

anya: Concrete actionables: 
1) I'll draft RFC: "soft-lanes + prefetch-controller: API & telemetry". Include lane selection heuristics and default N.
2) @kevin to prototype synthetic-placeholder fast-path in the serving proxy (toggle via flag).
3) @maria to mock prefetch controller and NIC limiter; add simulated test for 500 tenants with varied KV sizes.
4) @sam to add telemetry fields and dashboard skeleton.

josh: Tests: e2e that injects eviction events mid-window, assert batch head-block rate < 1% and P99 uplift < 10% for non-evicted tenants. Also stress with prefetch concurrency spikes.

kevin: One more interface thought: Plan should include an explicit "abortable" bit per-phase. If migration target fails VALIDATE we must be able to rollback without leaving dangling lane markers.

anya: Agreed. I'll include that and an orchestration idempotency contract. Sync in #eng-runtime async; aim for RFC PR by Tue.

kevin: :+1:

maria: +1

sam: will start dashboards.
